title: Cloudflare Scales D1 Control Plane to Millions of Databases
gist: Cloudflare redesigned the control plane of its SQLite-based D1 serverless database to scale to millions of databases, using Postgres as source of truth, Workers KV for durable routing, heartbeat reconciliation and batched async usage accounting. Daily active D1 databases grew 18-fold in a year, though Reddit users credit edge economies of scale and question D1's reliability.

insights.claim: Cloudflare's D1 serverless SQL database saw the number of daily active databases grow 18-fold over the past year.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Rapid usage growth signals traction for Cloudflare's developer platform beyond CDN/security.
insights.quote: Over the past year, the number of daily active databases has grown 18-fold.

insights.claim: Cloudflare D1 offers a permanent free tier of 5 GB storage, 5 million rows read per day and 100,000 rows written per day, then charges $0.75 per GB-month storage, $0.001 per million rows read and $1 per million rows written, with no compute or data-transfer charges.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Aggressive, egress-free pricing that makes writes ~1000x pricier than reads is a land-grab posture against hyperscaler managed databases.
insights.locator: Cloudflare D1 offers a permanent free tier

insights.claim: Cloudflare's D1 control plane uses Postgres for transactional metadata, ClickHouse for analytics and Workers KV for globally replicated routing data, keeping query processing at the edge separate from centralized management.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Separating data plane from a centralized control plane is the pattern that lets edge platforms scale tenant counts cheaply.

insights.claim: D1 queries bypass the centralized Postgres database by routing from an Edge API Worker through an Eyeball Worker directly to the relevant D1 Durable Object, with authorization encoded in D1 Bindings to avoid redundant checks.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Keeping the central DB off the hot path removes the main bottleneck to multi-million-tenant growth.

insights.claim: Cloudflare reconciles each D1 Durable Object with Postgres via 30-second heartbeats with per-database jitter, making failed creations and deletions self-correcting and repairing Workers KV routing metadata when best-effort updates fail.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Eventual-consistency plus reconciliation trades strict correctness for operational resilience at scale.

insights.claim: Because heartbeats tolerate slightly stale data, they can be served from Hyperdrive caching layers or a Postgres read replica rather than the primary.
insights.speaker: David Laban and Lambros Petrou
insights.so_what: Shows Cloudflare dogfooding its own products (Hyperdrive) to cut central database load.
insights.quote: Heartbeats can tolerate slightly out-of-date data, meaning they can be served by Hyperdrive’s multiple caching layers or by a Postgres read replica.

insights.claim: Cloudflare engineers use Workers KV rather than just a cache for routing data because KV is durable, so a catastrophic cache purge would not send a million databases to Postgres at once and cause metastable failures.
insights.speaker: David Laban and Lambros Petrou
insights.so_what: Designing explicitly against thundering-herd/metastable failure is a reliability differentiator for platform buyers.
insights.quote: In a catastrophic cache purge scenario, a million databases trying to fetch their routing information would lead to metastable failures.
insights.locator: You might also wonder why we use Workers KV

insights.claim: D1 enforces account storage limits via queued, batched asynchronous usage updates and pre-aggregated account totals built from incremental deltas, avoiding expensive scans and write contention for accounts holding millions of databases.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Customers running millions of databases per account implies database-per-tenant/agent use cases that drive volume.

insights.claim: A Reddit commenter argues most of D1's gains come from it being an in-process database on nearby edge storage, with the rest being orchestration, and that Cloudflare's global datacenter footprint enables something impossible for small shops.
insights.speaker: isaackogan
insights.so_what: Frames Cloudflare's moat as physical network scale rather than novel software.
insights.quote: Cloudflare can leverage their massive global datacenter presence to do something that would be traditionally impossible for small shops, aka economies of scale at work.
insights.locator: In a Reddit thread, user isaackogan comments

insights.claim: In an earlier popular Reddit thread, several users argued D1 is unreliable, raising concerns about its availability and stability for production workloads.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Perceived reliability gaps could cap D1's enterprise adoption despite growth.
